newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar opens firmer after inflation data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar opens firmer after inflation data.

text.p: * Canada's dollar opened firmer in light trading on Thursday at C$1.3731 (US$0.7282) after the release of economic data showing a slight increase in Canada's core rate of inflation, dealers said. * They said the core consumer price index, which jumped to 2.0 percent on the year, prompted interest to buy Canada dollars on speculation of an imminent rate hike.
The Canadian dollar opened firmer in light trading on Thursday at C$1.3731 (US$0.7282) after the release of economic data showing a slight increase in Canada's core rate of inflation, dealers said.

Statistics Canada reported that the unadjusted consumer price index (CPI) for June rose 0.2 percent in the month and 1.8 percent in the year. The core CPI, which excludes the volatile food and energy components, rose 2.0 percent.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast the seasonally adjusted CPI to rise 0.1 percent on the month and the unadjusted CPI to rise 0.1 percent on the month.
The survey also forecast a 1.7 percent year-over-year rise in the all-items index and 1.8 percent rise in the core CPI.
Analysts said the upward blip in core CPI prompted some interest in the market to buy Canada dollars on speculation that the Bank of Canada might raise interest rates.

"Some people are reading the inflation numbers as possibly triggering a Bank tightening, and they bought a little bit of Canada (dollars)," said Stephen Wateridge, managing director of corporate foreign exchange for CIBC Wood Gundy.
"But that's not our read of the numbers, which we thought looked pretty good," Wateridge added.
Traders said the Canadian dollar's recent technical weakness at the C$1.3755 (US$0.7270) level had tapered off with buying interest beginning to pick up.
"With the technical sell-off in the Canada (dollar) complete, look for the Canada (dollar) to regain some lost ground," said one trader with a Canadian bank.

"We'll probably try to nudge a little lower, perhaps down to C$1.3715 (US$0.7291). Given the numbers we've had out of the U.S. this week, there's no real reason why we shouldn't see the Canada (dollar) rally back below the figure of the next few days," Wateridge said.
Analysts said the release of Canadian trade numbers on Friday would be the next hurdle for the Canadian dollar.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar rose against the German mark to 1.3069 marks from 1.3033 marks at Wednesday's close, and climbed to 84.54 Japanese yen from 84.05 yen.
